title: Mansa Musa’s Golden Pilgrimage: How a 1324 Hajj Redefined Mali
hook: When the richest man of his age trekked across the Sahara with a caravan of gold, the world took notice—and the Mali Empire never looked back.
logline: Mansa Musa’s 1324 pilgrimage to Mecca dazzled the Mediterranean, reshaped trans‑Saharan trade, and set the stage for Mali’s cultural flowering.

chapters.title: The Wealth of the Sahel
chapters.purpose: Establish Mali’s economic base and its role in the trans‑Saharan gold trade.
key_events: Mali controls gold mines of Bambuk and Bure, feeding the Sahara’s caravan routes.
National Geographic notes Mali’s prosperity tied to African trade networks.

chapters.title: The Pilgrimage Begins
chapters.purpose: Show the planning and departure of the 1324 hajj, linking political ambition with religious duty.
key_events: Mansa Musa assembles a massive caravan, escorted by Seydou.
The journey routes through the desert toward Cairo, as described by the Met Museum’s Sahel exhibition.

chapters.title: Gold Floods Cairo
chapters.purpose: Illustrate the immediate economic shock in the Mediterranean and its diplomatic reverberations.
key_events: Musa’s arrival in Cairo (1324‑25) with a “very large quantity of gold” disrupts local markets (Metropolitan Museum, gold‑trade essay).
Ibn al‑Khalil records soaring prices and the need for the vizier to intervene.

chapters.title: From Pilgrimage to Patrimony
chapters.purpose: Connect the pilgrimage’s fame to Mali’s cultural legacy, especially Timbuktu’s rise as a scholarly hub.
key_events: Musa’s return spurs diplomatic gifts and builds prestige across the Islamic world.
Metropolitan Museum notes his patronage helps seed Timbuktu’s development as an Islamic learning center (while cautioning that no single ruler created it).
Al‑Bukhari’s manuscript collection begins to attract scholars, cementing Mali’s reputation.

ending: The gold‑laden caravan may have emptied the Egyptian market, but it filled Mali’s name into every merchant’s ledger, turning the empire into a beacon of wealth and learning for generations.
